learning: If oscillation falls and the slalom improves with the controller held, the mass lever is confirmed and kd or kp can be tuned next. If the slalom still stalls at max_error near 0.06 m with line losses at or below 2, the next lever is sensing reach (spread) rather than gain. If the s-bend completion drops, mass alone is not enough and the controller needs its own change.
notes: Complete robot with the Builder's 0.6 kg geometry and the iteration-2 controller, unchanged. The controller is held constant so the race isolates the mass change. The result will show whether lower yaw inertia cuts oscillation and slalom error.
rationale: The Builder's proposal changes only the mass, from 0.8 to 0.6 kg, which lowers yaw inertia by about 25 percent. Iteration 2 (base_speed 1.3, kp 2.4, kd 0.5) is the best controller so far: the oval finishes 20 of 20, the s-bend finishes 6 of 20, and the slalom finishes 0 of 20 with progress 0.10 and max_error 0.0628 m. Line losses are 0.55 to 1.0 per run, so sensing is not the limit. Speed barely matters on the slalom: progress was 0.136 at base 1.6 and 0.10 at base 1.3, so I am not lowering speed further. The oval's 0.206 steering oscillation is above the roughly 0.15 level the Integrator flagged, and the Builder expects the mass change to reduce it. To keep the race readable, I hold the controller at the iteration-2 values and change nothing except the geometry arriving from the Builder. This isolates the mass effect: any change in oscillation, slalom max_error or s-bend completion can then be attributed to mass. Expected, not measured: oval oscillation falls below about 0.15, and slalom max_error moves toward 0.06 m. The Builder's geometry is passed through unchanged, so the complete robot matches the proposal exactly.
